geography.title: The valley and its surrounding hills
geography.text: The Imphal Valley occupies the central part of Manipur, surrounded by hill systems. The state borders Myanmar and the Indian states of Assam, Nagaland and Mizoram.

geography.title: Water connects the landscape
geography.text: Loktak Lake lies in the valley. The Water Resources Department describes drainage from surrounding hills into the valley and onward toward the Chindwin system in Myanmar.

geography.title: Why the definitions matter
geography.text: Government publications use different definitions of flat valley and broader valley region. This atlas does not present a single hill-to-valley area ratio as a universal definition.

history.title: Central administration begins
history.text: The Public Service Commission's institutional history dates the beginning of centrally administered status to 15 October 1949.

history.title: Manipur attains statehood
history.text: Manipur attained statehood under the North-East Area (Re-organisation) Act, 1971.

events.title: Violence beginning in May 2023
events.text: The subsequent government inquiry explicitly covers violence on 3 May 2023 and thereafter. This entry establishes the inquiry's temporal scope, not a finding about responsibility.

events.title: Commission of Inquiry notified
events.text: The Union government notified an inquiry chaired by Justice Ajai Lamba to examine causes, spread and possible lapses by responsible authorities or individuals.

events.title: Relief supplies and committee coordination
events.text: The Court addressed essential supplies in relief camps and coordination of experts with the committee chaired by Justice Gita Mittal. Court directions are distinguished from findings on the underlying allegations.

events.title: President's Rule imposed
events.text: The date of imposition is documented in the Ministry of Home Affairs account of parliamentary approval. Broader claims made in the ministerial speech are not adopted as independent findings.

events.title: Elected government restored
events.text: Public broadcaster Akashvani reported revocation of President's Rule and the swearing-in of Yumnam Khemchand Singh as Chief Minister.

events.title: Supplementary demands presented
events.text: The state published the Chief Minister's speech for supplementary demands for grants for 2025–26.

events.title: State issues discussed with Union ministers
events.text: Akashvani reported meetings between Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh, Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Union Minister Kiren Rijiju. Proposed visits and project announcements in that report are not treated here as completed delivery.

events.title: Census deferral reported
events.text: Akashvani reported a Union government decision to defer Census operations following a review meeting. A primary judicial order and subsequent proceedings have not been indexed; this dated report does not establish the current legal position.

events.title: Labour welfare assistance distribution reported
events.text: Akashvani reported distribution of assistance to labour card holders, including support for education of children in relief camps. The report also relays government statements on rehabilitation; it does not independently establish the extent of return, recovery or scheme outcomes.

scenarios.title: Historical patterns persist
scenarios.assumption: The election-day party and candidate patterns of previous Assembly contests remain informative.
scenarios.test: Compare party retention, candidate continuity and margins over identical constituencies.
scenarios.limit: Conflict, defections and changes in candidate selection can break historical relationships.

scenarios.title: Greater fragmentation
scenarios.assumption: More parties or independents attract substantial candidate votes.
scenarios.test: Track party-level vote concentration, effective number of parties and seat-to-vote differences.
scenarios.limit: A statewide swing cannot determine each constituency result; alliances and candidates matter.

scenarios.title: Regional parties gain influence
scenarios.assumption: Regional parties and independents become more important in representation or coalition formation.
scenarios.test: Compare their verified seat totals, vote shares and public coalition agreements.
scenarios.limit: Coalition arithmetic is not a probability model and does not imply a common community preference.

scenarios.title: Participation changes
scenarios.assumption: Turnout and access differ from earlier elections.
scenarios.test: Use official electors, votes-polled and turnout denominators; document disrupted participation.
scenarios.limit: Turnout change alone cannot identify individual voter movement or party conversion.

scenarios.title: Coalition arrangements differ
scenarios.assumption: Parties form different pre-election or post-election arrangements.
scenarios.test: Distinguish election-day wins from subsequent support, mergers, defections and by-elections.
scenarios.limit: Hypothetical combinations are not endorsed, predicted or assigned numerical probabilities.
